newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ukraine signs European accord scrapping executions.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine signs European accord scrapping executions.

text.p: Ukraine on Monday signed a European accord to abolish the death penalty, a move hailed by officials as a major step towards stamping out capital punishment in Europe.
Ukrainian Deputy Foreign Minister Anton Buteyko signed protocols to the European convention on human rights, scrapping torture as well as the death penalty, the council said in a statement.
"The signature...by Ukraine, and by Russia three weeks ago, is a crucial step towards abolishing the death penalty in Europe," said the council's Secretary General Daniel Tarschys.
But the move must still be ratified by the Kiev parliament, the council said.

The 40-member council, which promotes democracy and human rights across Europe, had in January threatened to bar Ukraine's delegates unless it quickly honoured commitments to halt executions and abolish the death penalty within three years.
Ukraine had initially pledged to stop executions in 1995, at the time it joined the council, but 196 prisoners were executed in 1996, according to human rights group Amnesty International.
However no executions have been carried out so far in 1997. Abolition of the death penalty is in theory a condition of membership.
In signing the protocol, Ukraine became the seventh Council of Europe member to agree to scrap executions without formally ratifying the action, council officials said.
